newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Briton killed by man who gave him lift in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Briton killed by man who gave him lift in Israel.

text.p: A British hitchhiker was shot dead and his girlfriend was wounded in Israel's southern Negev desert on Wednesday by a motorist who gave them a lift.

Police said the two tourists had hitched a ride at a gas station in the Red Sea resort of Eilat. The driver who picked them up shot them during a stop 120 km (80 miles) north of the resort at about one a.m. and had then driven off.
"We were having a cigarette outside the car, like a rest from the journey, and then I just saw lots of flashes and he'd shot us basically," Charlotte Gibb, 20, told reporters.

"There was silence, we weren't really speaking, and then I just saw the light," Gibb said at Soroka hospital in the town of Beersheba, where doctors carried out surgery on bullet wounds to her cheek, right hand and left arm.

The British consulate in Tel Aviv named the dead man as Jeffrey Max Hunter, a 22-year-old law student from Surrey south of London. It said Gibb, a student from the town of Peterborough, was not in a critical condition.
Police said the driver may have fled to Egypt.
"We do not exclude the possibility that the car has fled to the south towards the Egyptian border and probably crossed it," a police spokeswoman said.
The motive for the shooting, the second attack involving young British tourists in Israel in three weeks, was unclear.

Deputy police commander Dudi Cohen told Israel Radio that police were checking all leads but had little to go on. "The description given by the woman is the only thing we have. It is a partial description, even 'partial minus'," he said.
Gibb told reporters that the driver spoke Hebrew but that she did not know whether he was an Israeli Jew or Arab.

Several teenagers among a group of visiting British school students were slightly injured in Jaffa last month by an Israeli Arab who rammed into them with his car and then chased them down a street brandishing a Samurai sword.
Police said that assailant, who was arrested at the scene, had been bent on avenging the pasting in the West Bank town of Hebron of a poster depicting Prophet Mohammed as a pig.
An Israeli court ruled on Wednesday that the woman who put up the posters, 26-year-old Israeli Tatyana Suskin, was mentally fit to stand trial.
